info.title: darkmux client API
info.description:
# Using the darkmux client API

`darkmux client serve` is the API an app (Mux Bot, or your own) uses to pair with a Mac and run work on it. This page is the order of calls and what to do on each outcome. The routes, request bodies, replies and refusal codes themselves are in the OpenAPI document this page opens (`GET /client/openapi.json`), and this page does not repeat them.

## Where an app reaches it

- **On the Mac:** `darkmux client serve` listens on 127.0.0.1 only. An app on the same Mac connects there.
- **From another device on the tailnet:** when the Mac's operator has turned remote use on, the same API is also at the Mac's tailnet address, through Tailscale. An app on the Mac learns it from `GET /client/whoami`: when `remote` says `available`, its `url` is the address to hand the other device (a QR code, a share sheet).
- Anything else (another proxy, or a web page, which sends an Origin header) is refused `not_local`, or `not_forwarded` while the tailnet address is up.

## Pair on the Mac

1. Make a random pair secret and keep it in memory. Send `POST /client/pair` with a code your app shows its user and that secret. The reply names a request.
2. Show the code. A Mux Bot signed by a verified team is approved at once. Any other app waits for the operator, who approves it in a dialog on the Mac or with `darkmux client approve --code <CODE>`.
3. Poll `GET /client/pair/{request_id}` with the secret in `X-Pair-Secret`:
   - `pending`: keep polling.
   - `approved`: the reply carries the token, this once only. Store it (below) before anything else.
   - `denied`: stop, and tell the user the Mac said no.
   - `expired`: no one approved it in time. Start again from step 1.
   - `not_found`: the request is gone (the wrong secret, a token already collected, or a request expired long ago). Start again.
4. A pairing request answered `too_many_requests` found the queue full. Wait, then start again.

## Pair from another device over the tailnet

Gate this on the app on the Mac: offer it only when that app's `GET /client/whoami` lists `remote_requests` in `capabilities` and `remote` says `available`.

The calls are the ones above, sent to `url`. What differs:

- **It always waits for the operator, who compares your code.** Nothing on the device can approve it. The dialog and `darkmux client approve` show the tailnet user and device the request names, and tell the operator to approve only if that device shows your code. A program on the Mac can send a request that names any device, so the code on your screen is what tells the operator the request is yours: show it large, from the moment the pairing starts until it ends.
- **Only the Mac's own tailnet user pairs.** A request from another user of a shared tailnet is refused `remote_user_not_owner`, naming the user who may. When Tailscale on the Mac cannot say who that is, the request answers `unavailable`: try again later.
- **Tailscale must confirm the user.** The user and device recorded come from Tailscale, never from the body, and Tailscale's own record of the device must name the same user as the request: otherwise it is refused `remote_identity_unconfirmed`. A device logged in to Tailscale with a tag has no user and is refused `remote_identity_missing`: log it in as a user. When Tailscale on the Mac cannot say which device sent the request, it is refused `remote_device_unknown`: try again later.
- **A device has at most two pairing requests waiting.** A third is refused `too_many_requests` (it never replaces an earlier one): wait for one to end.
- **Poll from the same device, as the same user.** A poll from another user is refused `remote_identity_mismatch`, from another device `remote_device_mismatch`, and neither uses up the token.

## Keep the token

- Store it in the platform's secure store (the Keychain on Apple platforms), never in a log, a file or a URL. Send it as an HTTP bearer token on every route but the two pairing ones.
- A device paired over the tailnet is answered through `url` only as the tailnet user and from the device it paired as. From another of the user's devices it is refused `remote_device_mismatch`, as another user `remote_identity_mismatch`. Tell the user which, and do not discard the token.
- The token is still a bearer token: it is not usable only from that device. Sent from a program on the Mac itself, it is answered as an app on the Mac. Guard it as you would a password.
- `not_paired_remotely` means the token was paired on the Mac, so it works there only. Pair the device over the tailnet.
- `unauthorized` means darkmux does not know the token: the operator revoked it (`darkmux client revoke`), on the Mac and remotely at once. Delete it and pair again.
- Pairing again makes a new client with a new token. The old one keeps working until the operator revokes it, and its workspaces stay with it: the operator gives one to the new client with `darkmux client claim`.

## Check what this darkmux can do

After pairing, call `GET /client/whoami` and gate every feature on its `capabilities`, never on `version`. A darkmux with no `capabilities` at all predates the list. A capability says what the build can do, not what this Mac allows: a preview may still be refused `preview_disabled`, and remote use is on only while `remote` says `available`.

## Read a refusal

Every refusal carries a `code` and an `error`. Branch on the `code`; show the `error` to a person; never parse it. `unavailable` means not now (the Mac's settings could not be read, or `darkmux client serve` is stopping): send the request again later. `too_many_requests` means slow down. A code your app does not know comes from a newer darkmux: handle it by the HTTP status class.

## Run work

1. Optionally list what may run with `GET /client/profiles`.
2. Make or reuse a workspace with `POST /client/workspaces`, and name it in the run.
3. Start the run with `POST /client/work`. The reply names it.
4. Poll `GET /client/work/{work_id}` until its `status` is `done`, `error` or `cancelled`. While it is `running`, `activity` may say `starting_model` or `queued`: show that rather than a stall.
5. To stop it, `POST /client/work/{work_id}/cancel`, then poll on through `cancelling` until it ends.
6. Whatever a run changed is committed when it ends, however it ends. To take a finished run's changes back, `POST /client/work/{work_id}/undo` reverts them in a new commit; it is refused while a later run changed the same files, or another run works in the same workspace. `POST /client/work/{work_id}/keep` and `POST /client/work/{work_id}/discard` are for older apps: keep only reports the commit, and discard is an Undo.
7. A follow-up run in the same workspace names the run it `continues` from.
8. Read the result while `darkmux client serve` still holds it: a run is forgotten an hour after it ends, and at once if `darkmux client serve` restarts. A `not_found` for a run you started means it was forgotten.

## Workspaces and previews

- Look at a workspace with `GET /client/workspaces/{name}` and at what its runs changed with `GET /client/workspaces/{name}/changes`. A hand edit goes in with `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/edit`, an image with `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/image`.
- Remove one with `DELETE /client/workspaces/{name}`. It is refused while a run, an Undo or a preview holds it, and refused `unsaved_commits` when it holds commits kept nowhere else, until the user agrees to `force` it.
- Start a preview with `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/preview`, poll `GET /client/workspaces/{name}/preview` until it is ready or has failed, and stop it with `DELETE /client/workspaces/{name}/preview`. A preview also stops when it sits idle, when the app is revoked and when `darkmux client serve` stops, so read its status instead of assuming it still runs.
- A workspace with no preview recipe is refused `no_recipe`. For a cloned repository whose user approves one, `PUT /client/workspaces/{name}/recipe` sets it, when `recipe_set` is listed.
- A preview's address is on the Mac's loopback. A device on the tailnet opens it through a link instead (below).

## See a preview from another device over the tailnet

Gate this on `remote_preview` in `capabilities`, with `remote` `available`. A device paired over the tailnet sees one of its previews in its browser, through `url`:

1. Start the preview and poll it until it is ready, as above.
2. Send `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/preview/link` through `url`, with the device's token. The reply's `url` is a link to that preview for this device: it opens once, within `expires_in_secs`. Open it in the device's browser at once, and never keep or log it. From an app on the Mac it is refused `tailnet_only` (the preview's own address serves it), and for a preview that is not ready, `conflict`.
3. The browser opens the link (`GET /client/preview-link/{code}`). darkmux checks the request comes from the tailnet user and device the link was made for, sets a session cookie in that browser and sends it on to the root of `url`, where the preview is. Every path outside /client/ there is the preview's, its WebSocket upgrades included, so live reload works when the preview's reload socket uses the app port.
4. A link opened a second time, or too late, answers `not_found`; one whose preview stopped or restarted since it was made, or whose device was revoked, `conflict`. From another device or user it answers as a token would (`remote_device_mismatch`, `remote_identity_mismatch`), and is used up all the same. Ask for a new link.
5. The session lasts while its preview runs. It ends when the preview stops or restarts, when the device is revoked, when previews are turned off on the Mac, and when `darkmux client serve` stops: the preview's pages then answer `no_preview_session`, and an open WebSocket closes within a second. Ask for a new link and open it.

What that means for a preview:

- A browser holds one session for the Mac's address, so it shows one preview at a time: opening a link to another preview replaces it.
- The preview's own paths under /client/ answer as darkmux's routes, not the preview's.
- Its server gets requests with its own loopback address as their host and origin, without the device's token, the session cookie or Tailscale's headers. The rest of what the browser sends reaches it as sent: the referrer and fetch metadata name the tailnet address, and the browser's other cookies for the Mac's address (another preview's, or a service's on another port of that address) go with every request.
- It cannot set the session cookie, nor a cookie for other hosts (one with a Domain). Its answers are never cached (each is sent no-store, whatever the preview says), and it cannot register a service worker (refused `forbidden`).
- Only the browser's own requests to the Mac's address reach it: one from another origin or another site, a WebSocket included, is refused `forbidden`. Every tailnet address is the same site to a browser, so this, not the cookie, is what keeps another tailnet page out.
- A page of the preview counts as asking about it, so the idle check does not stop a preview while it is open.
- At most six of a page's requests reach the preview at once (the rest wait their turn, as a browser's own connection limit makes them), and at most two WebSockets stay open (another answers `too_many_requests`). A request the preview does not begin to answer within three minutes answers `unavailable`.

**Previews share one origin.** Every preview is served at the same address, so the browser treats them as one site. Opening a link clears that address's cache and storage, but a tab still open on preview A, or storage the browser keeps for the address, can still reach preview B once B's session is set: A's page would then be talking to B. Show each preview in a web view of its own, with a data store of its own (on Apple platforms, a web view whose data store is made for that preview with WKWebsiteDataStore(forIdentifier:)), and close a preview's web view before opening another's link.

parameters.name: X-Pair-Secret
parameters.description: The `pair_secret` the pairing request sent. Without it, or with another, the request is unknown (404).

303.description: The preview session is set in this browser: on to the root, where the preview is.

Set-Cookie.description: The preview session cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/.

oneOf.description: Not from an app on this machine (a proxy, another host, a web page).

(#3560) Not from an app on this machine, and not through the tailnet
entry this `client serve` published either (another proxy, or a
`Host` other than the entry's name and port). Only answered while
the entry is up (`whoami.remote.state` `available`); otherwise such a
request is `not_local`.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry with a valid token, but the token's
pairing recorded no tailnet identity (it was paired on the Mac): the
device must pair over the tailnet. The token still works on the Mac.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry, a pairing, its poll, or a request
with a valid token, but Tailscale named no tailnet user for it: a
tagged device (Tailscale sends no user for one), or a login that is
not valid UTF-8 (sent empty). A Funnel request never gets here: it is
`not_forwarded`.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry with a valid token (or polling a
pairing), from a tailnet user other than the one the device paired as.

(#3560) No longer sent: darkmux stopped sending it when pairing over
the tailnet landed. Kept only because the wire contract only grows
from 5.0 on.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry, but Tailscale's own record of the
device at the forwarded address names another tailnet user than the
request's `Tailscale-User-Login` (or none): the request did not come
from that user through Tailscale as it says.

(#3560) A pairing through the tailnet entry from a tailnet user other
than the one this Mac is logged in to Tailscale as: only that user's
devices may pair over the tailnet.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry, but Tailscale on the Mac could
not say which tailnet device the request came from (its `whois`
failed, or named none), so it cannot be checked against the device a
token was paired from, or recorded for a pairing. Refused, never
guessed; try again once Tailscale answers on the Mac.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry with a valid token (or polling a
pairing), from another tailnet device than the one it was paired
from, even one of the same user's.

(#3560) A route only a device paired over the tailnet uses through the
tailnet entry (asking for a preview link, or opening one), called
from this machine instead. An app on this Mac opens the preview's own
loopback address.

(#3560) Through the tailnet entry, on a path outside `/client/` (a
preview's), with no preview session cookie, or one whose session has
ended: its preview stopped or restarted, its device was revoked, or
`client serve` restarted. Ask the app for a new preview link.
No such route, id or workspace.
A missing or unknown bearer token.
Outside what this machine lets an app run (a profile, a workdir).
The state does not allow it now (not running, already undone).
Valid JSON that cannot be acted on as asked.
Too many pending pairings or running work items.

Not now: this machine's config could not be read, or `client serve`
is stopping (send the request again once it is back).
darkmux failed; its log says why.
`clients.preview.enabled` is off on this machine (403).

A worktree with no recorded checkout of the user's, or no longer a
worktree of it: no checkout of theirs to read a recipe from (404). A
clone of a repo URL answers `NoRecipe` instead (#3571).

A template project whose first commit, the recipe a preview of it
trusts (#3460), has no `.darkmux/preview.json` (404).
No `.darkmux/preview.json` in the user's checkout (404).
The recipe cannot be used as written (422).

The repository's own git config defines a filter driver darkmux
does not run (#3457).

The checkout's own git config sets a network key darkmux does not
read; the fetch was refused (#3457).
Fetching the checkout's remote failed for another reason.
Cloning the repository failed.

The workspace is not on a `mux/` branch of its own (a clone made
before clones got one, left on the default branch or the ref it was
cloned at), so a PR or backup from it would push onto that branch
(409); its next run moves it onto one.

Removing the workspace would lose commits nothing else holds (a
clone's branch, a template project's history; 409): save them, then
remove it with `force`.
The memory is held by a running dispatch; retry later.
The model does not fit this machine; retrying cannot help.

(#3510) The memory is held by programs darkmux did not start; retry
once they free it.
The engine server would not start, or exited.
darkmux's own engine server would not stop to make way.
A server darkmux did not start holds the endpoint's port.
No engine binary, or a version darkmux was not verified against.
The engine's own server is running (rec runs one per machine).

The run failed with no code of its own (it exited, was killed, or
printed no result).

ClientCode.description: Why the client API refused a request, or why a work item failed.

scopes.description:
Accepted for apps built against the first contract, and ignored: what
a paired app may run is this machine's `clients.profiles`.

PairPoll.description:
`GET /client/pair/{id}`: `pending`, `denied` or `expired`, or, once,
`approved` with the token.

ClientScopes.description:
What a paired app may run: `profiles` is this machine's
`clients.profiles`, or the word `"local"` when it is unset (any profile
whose work stays on this machine). `workspace` is always true.

version.description:
(#3494) This darkmux's version, for display and diagnostics. An app
gates a feature on `capabilities`, never on this.

capabilities.description:
(#3494) Every capability this darkmux's client API has, in
declaration order: exactly what it supports. A darkmux with no
`capabilities` field is 5.10 or 5.11; `ClientCapability`'s docs say
what each has and how to tell them apart. The preview ones are what
the build can do: `preview_disabled` still answers when this machine
has previews off.

remote.description:
(#3560) Whether this `client serve` is reached from other devices on
the tailnet, decided at its start (`clients.remote`).

via.description:
(#3560) How this request reached `client serve`: from an app on this
machine, or from a paired device through the tailnet entry.

id.description:
`m-` and 16 hex digits of a hash of the hardware uuid (never the
uuid itself): stable across renames and every device that pairs.

name.description: The fleet name (`DARKMUX_MACHINE_ID`, else the hostname).

ClientMachine.description: This machine, as `/client/whoami` and `/client/profiles` name it.

oneOf.description:
(#3486) `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/preview` takes `{"clean":
true}`: a clean restart, with a fresh install.

(#3460) `POST /client/workspaces` takes `template: true`: a new
project from a template repo, which previews from its first commit.

`POST /client/work` takes `continues`: a run that follows up on an
earlier run of this client's in the same work copy.

(#3571) A workspace cloned from a repo URL runs a preview, from the
recipe in the commit darkmux cloned.

(#3571) `PUT /client/workspaces/{name}/recipe`: the recipe a clone's
user approved, for a clone whose commit has none.

(#3545) `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/image`: an image added to a
workspace.

(#3533) `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/edit`: a hand edit of a text
span, committed like a run.

(#3520) `DELETE /client/workspaces/{name}`: a workspace removed, with
what darkmux made for it.

(#3560) `GET /client/whoami` carries `remote`: whether this machine's
`client serve` is published on its tailnet (`clients.remote
tailscale`), at which HTTPS URL, or why not. What the build can do:
`remote.state` says what this machine did.

(#3574) A model's `availability` (`GET /client/profiles`) carries a
`code` whenever a dispatch refusal fits, the same code that refusal
carries (`engine_in_use`, `engine_unavailable`, ...). With this
listed, a missing `code` means none fits; without it, the darkmux
predates codes and an app reads only `reason`.

(#3560) A device on the tailnet pairs through `remote.url` (approved
on the Mac, never on its own) and is then answered there with its
token, from the tailnet user and device it paired as. What the build
can do: `remote.state` says whether this machine is on the tailnet.

(#3560) `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/preview/link`: a one-time link
a device paired over the tailnet opens in its browser, through
`remote.url`, to see that ready preview at the entry's root. What the
build can do: `remote.state` says whether this machine is on the
tailnet, and `preview_disabled` still answers when previews are off.

ClientCapability.description: One thing the client API can do that an app may need to check for.

url.description: The HTTPS URL another device on the tailnet opens, when `available`.

reason.description: Why not, naming the fix, when `unavailable`.

ClientRemote.description:
(#3560) Where `client serve` stands on the tailnet, as `whoami` reports
it: what this process did at its start, from `clients.remote`. A request
through `url` is answered only for a paired device: its token, and the
tailnet user it paired as (`RequestVia::Tailnet`).

oneOf.description: `clients.remote` is `off`: this machine only, never published.
Published on the tailnet at `url`.

`clients.remote` asks for the tailnet, and `reason` says why it could
not be published; `client serve` serves this machine only.
From an app on this machine.

From a paired device on the tailnet, through `remote.url`: its token
checked, and its tailnet user the one it paired as.

ClientOpenApi.description:
(#3494) `GET /client/openapi.json`: this API's OpenAPI 3.1 document,
built from the route table (`client_openapi`).

model.description: The model the role's work would run on (the resolved selection).

endpoint.description:
`url` (an unmanaged server darkmux only sends to) or the managed
backend's name (`lmstudio`, `tensorfold`, `flint`).

reachable.description:
For a managed model (LM Studio, a server darkmux starts), darkmux can
make it resident now: its `availability` is `resident` or
`startable`. For a URL server, it answered just now.

loaded.description: The model is loaded and serving (`None`: couldn't tell).

error.description: Why it couldn't be described (e.g. not in the registry).

availability.description:
(#3466) Whether darkmux can make the model resident: `resident`,
`startable` (a stopped engine server darkmux would start),
`unavailable`, `external` (a server darkmux only sends to) or
`unknown` (a probe failed or ran out of time), with a reason for the
last two. `reachable` and `loaded` stay for older apps.

ClientProfileInfo.description:
One profile an app may run on this machine, as `GET /client/profiles`
reports it. Read-only: what the registry declares and whether its server
answers right now.

code.description:
(#3574) Why, for an app to branch on: the code a dispatch refusing
for the same reason carries (`dispatch.error`'s `payload.code`, the
client API's `ClientCode` spelling), so there is one vocabulary:
`engine_in_use` while rec's own server runs, `engine_unavailable`,
`port_in_use`, `model_start_failed`.
Absent when no dispatch refusal fits (a registry problem a dispatch
refuses before any engine is asked, a state that is not
`unavailable`). Additive (card schema 1.5): an older reader ignores
it, and a code a newer darkmux sends that this one does not know is
kept as its text.

Availability.description:
A model's availability and, for every state but `resident`, `startable`
and `external`, a one-line reason.

oneOf.description: Loaded or served now, at the profile's context.
Not resident, and darkmux can load it or start its server.
darkmux cannot make it resident; the reason says why.
An endpoint darkmux only sends requests to.

A probe failed or ran out of time; the reason names which. Never read
as `unavailable`. (#3450) Also a state a newer darkmux states that
this one does not know, as a peer's machine card may carry one.

AvailabilityState.description: Whether darkmux can make a model resident.

WorkAccepted.description: `POST /client/work`, 202: the run and the profile it resolved to.

profile.description: Absent or null: resolved as `darkmux dispatch <role>` would.

workspace.description: A workspace name (`POST /client/workspaces`), in place of `workdir`.

continues.description:
A Tweak: the id of this client's finished run in the same work copy
that this run follows up on.

title.description:
A short title for the run's commit message (default: the message's
first line).

activity.description:
(#3467) `starting_model` while the run's dispatch is starting its
model (an engine server, a load), and (#3504) `queued` while it
waits for a busy endpoint or memory, as the run lifecycle decides
it (the same `activity` `GET /runs` and `run list --json` carry).
Absent otherwise.

activity_elapsed_ms.description: With `activity`: how long the start (or the wait) has taken so far, ms.

result.description: The dispatch's own `--json` envelope (that verb's contract).

commit.description: The run's commit (short id), `null` when nothing was committed.

changes_error.description:
Why the run's changes could not be read (`changes` is then
`null` and nothing was committed): never "no changes".

code.description:
(#3468) Why it failed, for an app: the code its run's
`dispatch.error` named (`busy`, `wont_fit`, ...), else
`dispatch_failed`.

commit.description: The commit (short id) holding what the run left.

commit_error.description: Why what the run left could not be read or committed.

oneOf.description:
What a run that failed or was cancelled had already changed in its work
copy. It is committed as that run's own commit, so the next run's commit
never carries it and Undo can revert it. Every field is absent when the
run changed nothing.

commit.description: The commit (short id) holding what the run left.

commit_error.description: Why what the run left could not be read or committed.

oneOf.description:
What a run that failed or was cancelled had already changed in its work
copy. It is committed as that run's own commit, so the next run's commit
never carries it and Undo can revert it. Every field is absent when the
run changed nothing.
A dispatch is starting its model (an engine server, a load).

(#3504) A dispatch is waiting for an endpoint or memory a running
dispatch holds (`fleet.busy_policy` `queue`).

RunActivity.description:
(#3467) What a running run is doing besides its turns. One wire spelling
per value; a new one is additive.

skipped.description:
Repositories the run made inside the work copy (`git init sub`),
left out of the snapshot and so of the run's changes and commit.

RunChanges.description:
What a run changed in its work copy, against its baseline: the files and
the unified diff (capped).

FileChange.description:
One file a run changed: lines added and removed (`null` for a binary
file).

DiscardReply.description:
`POST /client/work/{id}/discard` (older apps): an Undo, reported as the
files restored (`removed` is always empty: an Undo is a revert commit).

UndoReply.description:
`POST /client/work/{id}/undo`: the revert commit (short id) and the files
it put back.

RecipeReply.description:
`GET /client/recipe` and `PUT /client/workspaces/{name}/recipe`: the
recipe the workspace's preview runs, read where it is trusted from (the
user's own checkout, a template project's first commit, or a clone's
cloned commit or approved recipe), never from the workspace.

schema_version.description:
The recipe format's version; one newer than this darkmux reads is
refused.

from.description:
Where a new workspace started (a ref, or `<repo>@<ref>` for a
template). A clone or a worktree is on a new `mux/<bot>-<id>` branch
cut from there.

fetch_error.description: Why the fetch of a reused (or source) checkout failed.

repo_url.description: Clone (or reuse a checkout of) this repo.

source_path.description: Or start from this local checkout, as a git worktree on a new branch.

bot.description: The asking bot's name, for the workspace and branch names.

template.description:
`repo_url` is a template: make a new project from it (at `ref`) with
none of its history and no remote, named for the bot; never reuse a
workspace.

branch.description: The branch it was on, `null` when detached.

branch_removed.description:
Whether that branch is gone: a clone's or a template project's goes
with it; a worktree's `mux/` branch in the user's checkout only once
merged into another branch, or with `force`; a branch of the user's
never.

preview_stopped.description: Whether its live preview was stopped first.

force.description: Also remove what holds commits nothing else does.

BranchChanges.description:
`GET /client/workspaces/{name}/changes`: the branch's committed changes
against origin's default branch, for an app to open a PR itself.

BranchFile.description:
One file on the workspace's branch that origin's default branch lacks:
its content (base64) and mode, or `deleted: true`.

EditReply.description:
`POST /client/workspaces/{name}/edit` (#3533): a hand edit. `matches`
is how many places in the workspace's tracked files hold the old text
(counted up to 2). Exactly one: the file changed and was committed as a
work record, which `/client/work/{work_id}` reports and `/undo` reverts.
Any other count: nothing changed and every other field is `null`.

old.description: The text as the page shows it (whitespace is collapsed for the match).

new.description:
The text the page is to show instead: written as sent, except that
in a markup file what would read as markup is written as text,
escaped.

ImageReply.description:
`POST /client/workspaces/{name}/image` (#3545): an image added to the
workspace. `matches` is set only when `replace` was sent: how many places
held that reference (counted up to 2). Committed (`work_id` set): the
image is at `path` (repo-relative), the page reaches it at `url`, and
`/undo` reverts it. Not committed: a `replace` found other than once
(every other field `null`), or the same image already there with nothing
to point at it (`path` and `url` set, no `work_id`).

name.description: The picked file's name: only a hint for the name darkmux gives it.

replace.description: The image reference as the page reads it (an ``'s `src` attribute): its one place in the tracked files is pointed at the new image, in the same commit.

log_tail.description: The end of its log, when it failed.

stage.description:
(#3561) What a starting preview is doing that an app may show;
absent the rest of the time.

code.description:
Which step, for an app to branch on: `getting_node` (darkmux is
fetching and verifying the project's Node.js for a sandbox on this
machine, first use of that version only).

detail.description: The same for a person: `getting Node 26.13.1, first use only`.

PreviewStage.description: (#3561) A step of a preview's start that an app may show.

clean.description:
Stop the preview, delete its install record and the recipe's
`install.unless_exists` path in the workspace, then start it: a fresh
install.

url.description:
Open it in the device's browser at once: it opens once, within
`expires_in_secs`, from the tailnet user and device that asked for
it. It sets that browser's preview session and goes on to the
entry's root, where the preview is.

expires_in_secs.description: How long the link waits to be opened, in seconds.

PreviewLink.description:
(#3560) `POST /client/workspaces/{name}/preview/link`: a link for this
device's browser to that preview, through the tailnet entry.

recipe.description:
A `.darkmux/preview.json`, checked as strictly as one in a checkout
and refused (422 `recipe_invalid`) unless it holds: no key the
recipe format does not know, a `schema_version` this darkmux reads,
no `env_from_source` (a clone has no checkout of yours to copy from),
and at most 16 KB (16384 bytes) as JSON.

RecipeSetBody.description:
(#3571) `PUT /client/workspaces/{name}/recipe`'s body: the recipe the
user approved for a clone whose repo has none.

ClientError.description: Every refusal: the status says the class, `code` which refusal it is.
